content: Nitric oxide synthase 1 (NOS1), also referred to as neuronal nitric oxide synthase, is an enzyme encoded by the NOS1 gene in humans. This enzyme belongs to a family of synthases (NOSs) that facilitate the production of nitric oxide (NO) from the amino acid L-arginine. Nitric oxide functions as a chemical messenger with a wide range of roles throughout the body. In the brain and peripheral nervous system, nitric oxide exhibits characteristics of a neurotransmitter and is thought to play a role in processes such as long-term potentiation, which is critical for synaptic plasticity and memory formation. However, it is also implicated in neurotoxicity associated with conditions like stroke and neurodegenerative diseases. Additionally, nitric oxide is involved in the neural regulation of smooth muscle activity, including processes such as peristalsis and penile erection. Nitric oxide is a key mediator of endothelium-derived relaxing factor activity, which is essential for the regulation of blood pressure. In macrophages, nitric oxide contributes to tumoricidal and bactericidal actions. This is evidenced by the fact that inhibitors of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) can block these effects. It is important to note that neuronal NOS and macrophage NOS are distinct isoforms of the enzyme. Both the neuronal and macrophage forms of NOS are unique among oxidative enzymes in that they require multiple electron donors for their activity. These include flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), flavin mononucleotide (FMN), nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH), and tetrahydrobiopterin. Clinical Significance NOS1 has been implicated in the pathophysiology of several conditions, including asthma, schizophrenia, and restless leg syndrome. It has also been studied in relation to bipolar disorder and the effects of air pollution exposure. Interactions NOS1 has been shown to interact with DLG4 (discs large homolog 4) and NOS1AP (NOS1 adaptor protein), which may influence its functional roles in cellular signaling pathways.
